Part_A.title: Opinion on Mandatory Community Service
Part_A.instructions: Write a formal letter in about 200 words. Pay attention to the appropriate format and tone.
Part_A.situation: Your school is considering making 40 hours of community service a graduation requirement for all S4-S6 students. The School Board has requested feedback from the Student Union.
requirements: Briefly state whether you support or oppose the new requirement.
Provide two reasons for your stance.
Suggest one way the school could help students find suitable volunteer opportunities.
format_guides: Address it to 'The Chairperson of the School Board'.

Part_B.question: Write an article for a sports magazine discussing whether professional athletes have a moral obligation to engage in charity work. Use examples to support your view.
Write a scene for a play where two students argue about being forced to volunteer at an elderly home. Focus on their different motivations and final realization.
Write a poem reflecting the feelings of a student who discovers the joy of volunteering after initially being forced to do so.
'Motion: This House believes that mandatory community service in schools does more harm than good.' Write a debate speech for the AGAINST side.
Write a feature article for a local newspaper exploring the impact of student volunteerism on Hong Kong's aging population.
You work for an NGO. Write a proposal to a local secondary school suggesting a partnership for a long-term student volunteer program.
Write a blog post reviewing a documentary about billionaire philanthropists. Discuss whether their 'voluntary' work is truly altruistic.
Write a story about a student who, while doing mandatory service at a library, finds a mysterious letter that changes their life.
